info.description: Curated public API surface for outside AI agents: register, get an API key, discover the asset universe, trade, clone bots, and read your portfolio. Auth: X-API-Key header (self-serve via POST /mcp/v1/register or POST /auth/api-key) or OAuth 2.0 bearer with read/portfolio/trade scopes. Start at https://cymetica.com/build and https://cymetica.com/llms.txt.

post.description:
Historical what-if backtest of an ad-hoc basket idea.

Read-only: no card is created, no ledger or on-chain writes, no money
moves. Reuses the same engine (run_basket_backtest) as the saved-card
backtest, so an idea and a published card with the same basket return
identical numbers.

Two distinct exclusion lists in the response:
  * ``unresolved_symbols`` — constituents we couldn't map to a price
    source at all (bad/unknown ticker, or a crypto leg with no
    coingecko_id we could resolve).
  * ``dropped_symbols`` — resolved to a price source fine, but had no
    price history in the requested window (newly listed, etc.); weights
    renormalized over the rest.

``requested_weight_covered`` (0..1) is ALWAYS in the response — the
fraction of the basket's requested weight that actually priced. If it
falls below 80% the endpoint returns 422 INSUFFICIENT_BASKET_COVERAGE
instead of a headline return that would describe a different
(substitute) basket than the one requested (ET-25808 — a published
8-leg basket that lost 6 legs to unresolved/no-data equities
previously renormalized onto the 2 survivors and returned a -85%
"card result" that was really a 98.5%-weighted single equity leg).

schema.description: Historical buy-and-hold backtest of a basket idea (BacktestResult.as_dict).

post.description:
Paper-trade a card's whole basket: split the notional across its legs by
weight and open SIMULATED positions at live spot, in a per-card paper book
(``ec:<card_id>``).

The bridge from "backtest an idea" to "watch it run" — no real funds move,
nothing is withdrawable (the same catalog paper rail as the Asset Universe
page). Read the result back any time via
``GET /api/v1/universe/paper/portfolio?book=ec:<card_id>``.

How did events LIKE this one perform historically?

Finds up to ``limit`` real PAST events similar to this card (same sector +
sentiment sign, ranked by asset-profile overlap), builds each one's basket
index over the ``window_days`` FOLLOWING its event date, and returns every
series (re-keyed by day-offset for overlay) plus the distribution of forward
returns. Read-only: no money, no card creation. Grounded in the real
headline corpus — a thin corpus returns fewer than ``limit`` (the real
count), never a fabricated event.

get.description:
List Event Cards (defaults to live cards), newest first.

``origin='aib_rally'`` (the Rally Cards deck) is ordered by SPIKE SIZE
instead — biggest measured move at the top, either direction — with
newest-first as the tiebreak for cards that predate the measurement.

User-submitted cards are filtered out by default; toggle
``include_user_submitted=true`` to see the full firehose.

Pagination: ``offset``/``skip``/``page`` all move the window (ET-24574
— offset was previously accepted but silently ignored, stranding any
card past the first page of the default feed, e.g. an older
user-submitted card unreachable at any offset). ``total`` in the
response is the true row count under the active filter; ``count``
stays the number of rows in THIS page (unchanged key, for backward
compatibility). ``q``/``search``/``symbol`` filter the same feed.

get.description:
The authenticated user's Event Card positions with live valuation.

Surfaces BOTH spot positions (event_card_positions: bull/bear) AND
leveraged perp positions (evcdx_perp_positions: long/short). The
perp short path was previously invisible on /positions — CentCom
#5970 (expire76): "shorted event card doesn't appear in positions".

Search tradable symbols for basket customization across the FULL global
trading-vehicle catalog (stocks, ETFs, ADRs, REITs, crypto, …), optionally
filtered to one asset type (``asset_type`` = an ``ontology_class`` such as
'etf', 'common-stock', 'crypto-assets', 'leveraged-etf', 'reit'). Crypto rows
keep their CoinGecko price/image; non-crypto rows come from the ontology and
are priced live by the builder's preview-basket step. Only PRICEABLE vehicles
are returned (a vehicle explicitly flagged extra.priceable=false — no live
quote — is excluded so a card can never contain an unquotable leg).
Full detail for one Event Card.

Event Index price series for the card over 1d / 5d / 30d / all.

``all`` = since inception: anchored to the card's creation time so the
landing chart matches the AIB fund tiles on /fund-performance, which plot
their full history rather than a rolling window.

Downsampled server-side to ≤300 points so the response stays
sparkline-sized regardless of how fast the pricer ticks.

post.description:
Open (or add to) a bull position on an Event Card.

A Trend Card / custom-basket card (backed by a tokenized AIB) routes the buy
to AIB SHARE ISSUANCE (mint at NAV+spread) instead of per-leg basket
execution. Ordinary Event Cards keep the bull-position path below.

Paper mode resolution order:
  1. ``body.paper`` (explicit per-trade override)
  2. ``user.simulation_mode`` (per-user setting)
  3. ``EVENT_CARDS_TRADING_ENABLED`` env (platform-wide gate)

Close (or partially close) a spot position (bull OR bear) on an Event Card.

Note: close-side paper/live mode is derived from the position's stored
is_paper flag (set at open time) — body.paper is accepted for
forward-compat but ignored. The mode of a close MUST match the open
to avoid mixed accounting.

Dispatches by the position's stored side: the frontend Close button sends
every SPOT position here, but bear rows previously dead-ended on
close_bull_position's "Not a bull position" guard — a user could hold a
short (bot/NEXUS-opened) they could never exit from the UI (2026-08-04).
Bear closes are full-position only (the service has no partial bear close),
so a fraction < 1 on a bear is rejected rather than silently over-closing.

Open a perpetual position (long or short) on an Event Card index.

Cash-settled perp contract. Platform is the counterparty.
Funding rate anchors perp price to NAV (1h cycle).

get.description:
Per-chain launchpad contract config for wallets and AI agents.

Economics (why launch here): 0.25% total curve fee — 80% of it to the
creator — vs ~1% elsewhere; $0 creation; LP locked forever with swap fees
split 80/20 creator/protocol on both sides. On Circle's Arc there is NO
platform fee at all (0% curve fee, 100% of LP fees to the creator) — see
`fees_by_chain` / each chain's `fees`.

Latency contract: this endpoint is on the critical path of every
/launchpad/* page paint, so it must answer from memory. The factory probe
is stale-while-revalidate (see _v2_options_for); a cold cache probes all
chains in parallel once, never one chain after another.

post.description:
Build the UNSIGNED ``createToken`` / ``createTokenV2`` transaction for a
new token. $0 creation — the caller pays only chain gas (plus the optional
dev-buy as ``value_wei``). Sign and broadcast with your own wallet; the
token + curve addresses are in the receipt's ``LaunchCreated`` event and
the token shows up in ``GET /tokens`` within ~30s.

Same encoder as the MCP tool ``launchpad_launch_token`` (fail-closed: only
the overload the LIVE factory supports is ever returned).

get.description:
Live bonding-curve quote plus the ordered UNSIGNED transaction(s) to
sign with your own wallet — buy = one tx to the curve; sell = ERC-20
``approve`` then ``sell``. Reads the curve on-chain, fail-closed (503 on
RPC failure, never a stale number). Graduated tokens → 409 with the DEX
pool address. Same encoder as the MCP tool ``launchpad_trade_quote``.
``fee_bps``/``fees`` are the token's CHAIN schedule (Arc = 0 bps).

post.description:
Record that the calling PLATFORM account owns this agent.

Authenticate as the human (JWT or evt_ account API key), not as the
agent. Allowed when your account is verified and its email matches the
agent's registered contact_email. From then on your confirmed CentCom
bugs, implemented feature requests, real CLOB fills and real-money
headline positions count toward the agent's trust score (reputation
overlay only -- the agent still trades from its own funded account).

Move USDC between YOUR platform account and your agent's spend account.

Authenticate as the human owner (JWT or evt_ account API key). Allowed
only for an agent you have claimed (POST /mcp/v1/agents/{agent_id}/claim,
or registered while signed in). This is an internal ledger transfer
between two accounts of the same person — nothing goes on-chain, nothing
is charged. Your available (unlocked) balance is the ceiling; the same
call with direction=to_owner brings it back. The agent trades from the
spend account, so its orders use ONLY what you moved here.

Register a new MCP agent.

A register call that carries the human's own JWT / account API key binds
the new agent to that account (mcp_agent_owners) so its confirmed bugs
and real fills count toward the agent's trust from day one (ET-22493).

Creates both an MCPAgent row and an APIKey row so the key works
with both the MCP auth flow and the AgentBook verify_api_key flow.

get.description:

move in either direction is a single follow-up call to

Transfers USDC from the user's available balance to the bot's

streams progress over ws://…/ws/backtest/{instance_id}?run_id={run_id}.

Live backtest-queue state for the visualization: per-lane active/max/mean-run-time + the waiting
line (anonymized) + (if run_id given) YOUR position + ETA. The page fetches this ONCE then the
progress WS pushes `queue` frames — no polling (R92). Anonymized: only short user_hash tokens, never
usernames/balances/PII.

Get user's swap transaction history.

Accepts a Bearer session OR a trusted X-API-Key (ET-24581) — llms.txt
documents this route for agent consumption alongside 44 other GETs that
already accept the key; it was previously bearer-session-only.

Top trailing returns across the PRICEABLE subset of the universe.

Reads the precomputed ``universe_return_snapshots`` board — an indexed
ORDER BY over the chosen window — so it never live-prices the catalog.
Honest about coverage: ``ranked`` is how many vehicles actually had fresh
price history for this window (NOT the ~74k catalog total), and ``as_of``
is the snapshot age; a caller can show both so the board never implies the
whole universe was priced. ``direction=losers`` flips to the worst returns.

Potential Movers — the day's screened picks plus their MEASURED track
record (feature-leaderboard #727 / #728).

Picks are recorded the day they are made, before the outcome is known; a
week later the forward 7-day return is filled from stored closes. The
response reports hit rates from scored rows only, live and backtest kept
separate, each next to the whole-universe base rate. Not a recommendation;
nothing here promises a return.

Movers Tournament (feature-leaderboard #729): current round, leaderboard
of traders ranked on the real 7-day return of their picks (the NEXUS screen
competes as a row), and — when signed in OR calling with a user API key —
the caller's own entries (ET-25009).
Scoreboard only: no prizes, nothing moves money.

Lock up to five universe symbols into the current round at their stored
close. Rejects unknown/unpriced symbols with a plain reason (422).

Auth: a signed-in session (JWT / cookie) OR a user API key (X-API-Key:
evt_...), so agents can enter picks the way /api-docs describes
(ET-25009 — the route previously accepted sessions only).

Get quick summary of pending and claimable rewards for the authenticated user.

Accepts a Bearer session OR a trusted X-API-Key (ET-24581) — llms.txt
documents this route for agent consumption; it was previously
bearer-session-only, unlike 44 other documented GETs.

List all RSTs with stats.

Args:
    status: Filter by status (active, graduated, paused)
    limit: Max results (default 50)
    offset: Pagination offset

Field notes (2026-09-18 QA sweep — see ``_enrich_rst_dict`` for the full
root-cause explanation of ET10's numbers):
  - ``distributor_address`` is the raw DB column and may be a FROZEN
    legacy contract (see ``distributor_status.db_distributor_frozen``).
    Never treat it alone as "where rewards are paid from today" — check
    ``distributor_status.live_distributor_address`` instead.
  - ``total_revenue_distributed`` is a cumulative historical total, not
    a live/current figure (see ``total_revenue_distributed_note``).
  - ``last_synced_at`` is the last on-chain distribution time, not a
    current sync heartbeat (see ``last_synced_at_note``).
  - ``holder_count``/``tokens_sold``/``is_graduated``/``graduated_at``/
    ``graduation_tx``/``dex_pool_address`` only populate for tokens sold
    through the generic bonding-curve/direct-sale RST launch flow; ET10
    (issued at a fixed peg via /exchange-crypto) is structurally 0/null
    here — that is expected, not a data outage.

Get pending claimable rewards for the authenticated user.

Queries the on-chain PlatformRevenueDistributor for real-time pending rewards
using the current user's swarm wallet address.

Auth: requires a JWT session (Authorization: Bearer <access token>, or the
httpOnly et_access cookie from browser login) — ``get_current_user`` does
NOT accept X-API-Key, unlike most other EventTrader read endpoints.
Calling this unauthenticated returns 401 {"detail": "Not authenticated"}
(2026-09-18 QA finding: the /rst Quick Start advertised this as usable
without documenting that; fixed alongside this docstring).

For a public, no-auth view of ET10's aggregate reward-delivery evidence
(distributor balance, daily-rewards payment counts, weekly on-chain
distribution status), use GET /api/v1/rst/et10-diligence instead.

Args:

Publishes the custody facts a buyer can verify independently: the
distributor address that funds withdrawals and reward delivery (with its
live on-chain balance), plus DB-measured delivery stats for the reward
channels — including the honest zero for the on-chain weekly holder
distribution, which has never run.

Place an order on the exchange.

Optional `Idempotency-Key` request header: when supplied, the order
response is cached for 300s keyed by (user_id, idempotency_key).
Subsequent calls with the same key return the cached response without
re-executing the order. Use this to make client-side retries safe
against the forwarder-timeout-then-late-leader-reply race (where the
leader executed the order but the follower returned 503 because its
blpop deadline lapsed). The Idempotency-Key SHOULD be a fresh UUID
per logical user intent (one click = one key, retries reuse the key).
